title: A record is one row of its kind's table, with typed columns, and its links are rows of their relations' tables
when: Loads a clean product's data.
then: Expects a use case with its typed columns, its parent, product and domain, and its actor as a part row, a domain rule's statement, an applies link as a row, and no problems.

title: Data files hold one JSON object per line, sorted by key, columns in table order
then: Expects one object per line, rows sorted by key with numbers as numbers, columns in the table's order, empty columns left out, and a trailing newline.

title: Data files keep text as UTF-8, and a table file goes when its last row goes
then: Expects text kept as UTF-8, and no file for a table whose last row is removed.

title: A line that is not JSON, a column the table lacks and a file for no table are named by file and line
then: Expects each refused, naming its file and line.

title: A data file's line order and each line's column order do not change what it means, and a file that is not <table>.jsonl is ignored
when: Copies the clean product's data with each file's lines reversed and each line's columns reversed, next to a README.md.
then: Expects the same records, links and coverage, and no problems.

title: Data files are the same bytes whatever order the rows were written in
when: Writes the same rows in two orders, then reloads and rewrites them.
then: Expects the same bytes each time.

title: A technical record names the file that builds it and a test the file that runs it, each relative to the repo root
when: Handlers name files outside the repo root and a test's file does not name it.
then: `file` loads as given on every technical and test kind; the missing files are reported as technical-file-missing and the silent test proves nothing.

title: lathe add adds a record from its column flags and prints the row and the file
then: Expects the row added and printed with its file.

title: lathe set changes a record by its ID, and clears a column given empty
then: Expects the column changed, and the one given empty cleared.

title: lathe move moves a record and reports every row that changed with it
then: Expects the record under its new parent, and every row that moved with it reported.

title: lathe link and unlink link and unlink two records
then: Expects the link's row added, then removed.

title: lathe remove removes a record with its parts and its own links
then: Expects the record, its parts and its links gone.

title: lathe show shows a record with its parts, children and links
then: Expects the record's columns, parts, children and links both ways.

title: lathe show, list and next-id
The MCP tools are add, set, move, link, unlink, remove, show, list, next_id and check
then: Expects exactly those tools.

title: lathe add gives each table its columns as help, from the schema
then: Expects each column with its type and meaning from the schema description.

title: lathe add refuses a flag that is no column, or a value of the wrong type, as bad usage
then: Expects bad usage and no write.

title: The MCP tools take input schemas generated from the schema description, product kinds included
then: Expects each table's columns and types in the tools' input schemas, a product kind's too.

title: lathe add refuses a write the command layer refuses, printing the reason, and changes nothing
then: Expects every reason printed, an exit code of 1 and the data files unchanged.

title: The add tool returns the row added, and a refusal with its reason
then: Expects the row on success and every reason on a refusal.

title: No skill tells the Agent to write spec files by hand
then: Expects no skill to tell the Agent to edit data files, only to use the tools.

title: Every example in the skills names real tables, columns and relations, with values of the columns' types
then: Expects every example's table, columns and relation in the schema, with values of their types.

title: The reference says a domain is one business capability, and the domain-named-for-technology check calls it a vertical slice whose technology is its technical records
when: The reference is built.
then: The domain kind's description calls a domain one business capability, and the `domain-named-for-technology` check's explanation calls it a vertical slice whose technology is its technical records, linked from the kind's entry.

title: The modeling skill's first step finds the business capabilities and makes each a slice, with the questions that tell one from a layer
when: Reads the `model-a-domain` skill.
then: Expects its first section to find the business capabilities before any record is written, and to ask at least four questions that tell a capability from a layer.

title: Each domain says its subdomain type: core, supporting or generic
when: A domain is written with no subdomain type, and with one that is not core, supporting or generic.
then: The column is required and described; both rows are refused.

title: The migrations are numbered in order and recorded as applied
when: Applies the migrations to a fresh database.
then: Expects them numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on, each recorded with its name.

title: A product's own kind takes effect on the next load, with its own table
when: Declares a product kind and adds a record of it in one write, then asks to remove the kind while the record is left.
then: Expects the next load to have the kind and its record, placed under its domain, with no error, and the removal of the kind refused.

title: The row types in src/store/tables.ts match the schema
when: Renders the row types from the schema description.
then: Expects them to equal the committed `lathe/src/store/tables.ts`.

title: Every kind has an ID in the registry, a title and its parent columns
then: Expects each kind's table keyed by an ID that is a foreign key into the registry, a required title, a foreign key for each parent column, and a required parent column on every kind but product.

title: Each relation's pairs fit its link table's ends
then: Expects every relation to have pairs, each pair's kinds accepted by the link table's ends or their supertypes, and every supertype member a kind.

title: The server has no way to change the meta-model
when: Sends POST and PUT requests to `/api/spec` and to schema-like paths, and a write to a meta table, on the running server.
then: Expects them refused, and the migrations unchanged.

title: Which kinds are obligations, and which links design or prove a product's own obligation, come from the schema
given: A product with its own obligation kind, with a design relation, a proof relation and one with no role.
when: The product is loaded.
then: Coverage lists exactly the kinds flagged as obligations; a record reached by the design and proof relations is designed and proved, one reached only by the relation with no role is neither.

title: The schema describes every table and every column of a stored table
then: Expects a description on every table, and on every column of a stored table that is not a link table.

title: A product's own kind takes effect on the next load, with its own table
when: Declares a product kind and adds a record of it in one write, then asks to remove the kind while the record is left.
then: Expects the next load to have the kind and its record, placed under its domain, with no error, and the removal of the kind refused.

title: A product's own kind is listed after Lathe's, with its own label, stage and obligation, and Lathe's kinds keep theirs
given: A product with its own kind in the domain model.
when: It is loaded.
then: The product's kind comes after Lathe's, with its own label, stage, parent and obligation; Lathe's kinds are as in a product with no kinds of its own.

title: A product relation with a new name gets a link table of its own; one with Lathe's name adds only its pair
given: A product declares a pair for Lathe's `about` and a relation of its own.
when: It is loaded.
then: `about` gains only the new pair and Lathe's other relations are unchanged; the product's relation gets its own link table.

title: A kind declared twice is refused, naming its file and line and the line of the first
when: The same product kind is declared twice.
then: A primary-key refusal on line 2 of the declaration file, naming the kind and line 1.

title: A capability sits under a domain with a required whole-number position, and every use case sits under one of its domain's capabilities
when: A capability has no position, position 0 or a repeated one; a use case has no capability or another domain's ID.
then: All are refused.

title: A use case under a capability, and everything under it, belongs to the capability's domain and counts in its coverage
when: A use case is moved under another capability of its domain.
then: Everything under a capability carries its domain and the pattern none; after the move the domain and the coverage are unchanged.

title: A pattern sits under the product with its settings, and use cases or domains follow it
when: A domain follows the pattern; a requirement tries to.
then: The domain loads with no pattern problem; the requirement is refused.

title: A pattern rule is owed by each domain that follows its pattern, itself or through a use case, and proved there by one pattern rule test
given: One domain follows a pattern through a use case and has its rule test; another follows it itself with none.
when: It is loaded.
then: The rule is owed in both and proved only in the first; a second test for one rule and domain is refused; a test naming a non-follower is an error.

title: A use case has one flow, whose steps need a path and a position, fulfill its requirements, invoke a command or query, happen in a view and exchange with integrations
when: A product is loaded.
then: A flow sits under its use case and its steps need a path and position; steps load with their fulfills, invokes, happens_in and exchanges_with links.

title: A well-formed flow raises no step problem; a second flow, a repeated position, a step fulfilling another use case and a second invoke are refused
when: A second flow, a repeated position, a step fulfilling another use case and a second invoke are written.
then: No step-order problem on the good flow; each broken row is refused.

title: A UC requirement no step of its flow fulfills is reported as not designed
when: The only fulfills link to a requirement is removed.
then: A designed gap and a not-designed warning, for that requirement only.

title: An ID a record names in its text is kept as written, and makes no link
when: Loads records whose text names other records, one of them twice.
then: Expects the text kept as written, no links, and no list of named IDs on a record.

title: Text keeps every repeat as written, its own ID included
then: Expects a record's text to keep an ID named twice, and its own ID.

title: Only link tables link records: a link to a record that does not exist is refused, while text naming it is not
when: Loads a use case whose goal names a missing rule, then adds an applies link to it.
then: Expects the text accepted and the link refused as a foreign key.

title: A record's text naming another product's record is plain text: products are separate spaces
when: Loads two products, where a use case's text names a record of the other product.
then: Expects the text kept, no link from the use case, and no problem about the other product's ID.

title: A token that is the ID of a record is plain text, whatever its prefix: it is no link
then: Expects a use case's text naming another record kept as written, and no links.

title: A bare product or domain ID in plain text is kept as written
then: Expects a domain's description naming the product and the domain, in plain text and in a code span, kept exactly.

title: A bare product or domain ID in a code span is kept as written, code span and all
then: Expects the product's description to keep its code span.

title: Code spans and fences in text are stored exactly as written, spacing included
then: Expects a use case's notes, with a fence and code spans, kept exactly.

title: A token that is not an ID of this workspace is plain text and no problem
then: Expects text naming IDs that no record has, with unknown prefixes, to be kept and reported by nothing.

title: An ID in text that no record has is no warning: no check reads text for IDs
then: Expects no problem for a missing rule named in text, and `data-refused` as the engine's only problem of its own.

title: A token starting with a product's or domain's ID and '-' is plain text, and no problem when no record has it
then: Expects text naming missing IDs with the domain's prefix kept, and no problem about them.

title: A token with any other prefix, such as STD- or SYS-, is plain text too
then: Expects text naming STD- and SYS- IDs kept, and no problem about them.

title: No ID in text, known or not, is a warning: Lathe has no check that reads text for IDs
then: Expects no `unknown-id-in-prose` problem, and no problem naming an ID written in another record's text.

title: The engine loads the five stages in order and each kind's stage and position, with the product and open questions outside them
when: A product is loaded.
then: Five stages in order, each described; kind positions run stage by stage; only the product and the open question have no stage.

title: Every kind's stage is one of the schema's stages, and a product kind with no stage sits in none
given: A product kind with no stage.
when: It is loaded.
then: Every kind's stage is one of the schema's; the product kind has no stage and no position; the stages are unchanged.

title: A product places its own kind in one of the five stages, or none, and cannot add a stage or change one of Lathe's kinds
when: It is declared in each of the five stages, in none, in a stage that does not exist, and with the name of one of Lathe's kinds.
then: Each stage and no stage load and the stages are unchanged; the unknown stage and Lathe's name are refused.

title: Reads kinds, folders and relations from the schema, kinds in the schema's order
when: Builds the app's workspace from a product's schema description.
then: Expects kinds in the schema's kind positions, from product, domain and capability to question, and each kind's label, stage, folder, parents and required columns.

title: An entity sits under an aggregate and needs a role, a value object has no owner, and entities link to entities by has_one and has_many
when: The schema and the reference are read.
then: An entity sits under an aggregate with a required role, a value object has no owner and its constraints sit under it, the four field tables are parts, and has_one and has_many join entities, all described.

title: A well-formed domain model gives no entity problem, and each entity rule fails on its own data
when: A child is left unreached, a link crosses aggregates, a second root is added, a role is dropped and an entity links to itself.
then: No problems on the good model; entity-unreferenced, has-crosses-aggregate and refusals for the rest.

title: An entity's fields are its entity_field rows in position order, each with a name, a meaning, exactly one type and whether it is required
given: Entity fields written out of position order.
when: They are loaded.
then: The fields come back by position with name, meaning, type and required, and an optional column name and example; only entities have entity fields; a field with no type or two is refused.

title: An entity, event or read model with no fields is a coverage gap
given: An entity, an event and a read model with no fields.
when: They are loaded.
then: Each is a coverage gap.

title: Another aggregate is referenced by a field typed by it: a foreign key in its own domain, a plain ID from another domain
given: An entity with a field typed by another domain's aggregate.
when: Foreign keys are added within the domain and into the other domain.
then: The field and the same-domain key load; the cross-domain key is refused; a has_many into another aggregate is an error.

title: The Markdown gives the data model, then kinds with their tables, other tables, relations, folders and checks, each with an anchor
then: Expects the sections in order, an anchor for each kind, table, relation, folder and check, and every link inside the document to land on an anchor.

title: The reference script prints a product's reference, or writes it with --out
when: Runs the reference script for a product with its own kinds, with `--print` and with `--out`.
then: Expects the rendered reference in both.

title: The reference holds every kind, table, relation, folder and check of Lathe's schema
when: Builds Lathe's reference.
then: Expects a use case's facts, parents, children and ID convention, the obligation values, each kind's table with its columns, keys and references, a part table, relation pairs and roles, the folders in order, every check row in run order and the engine's own `data-refused`.

title: A product's reference shows its own kinds and relations and its own checks
then: Expects a product's own kind with its table and relation pair, and its own checks after Lathe's.

title: The committed REFERENCE.md is the reference as the reference script writes it
when: Renders Lathe's reference.
then: Expects it to equal the committed `lathe/REFERENCE.md`.

title: A product's own checks are held to the same rule, and Lathe's are all documented
then: Expects every kind, table and check of Lathe's described, and a product's own checks with their summary and explanation.

title: The reference reads each relation by its labels
when: Builds the default reference.
then: Expects each relation rule to carry its forward and reverse labels, the relations table to show both, and a requirement's links in to read as "Designed by" and "Proved by".

title: A domain event sits under an aggregate, a command under an aggregate raises and checks, and a policy under a command hears one event
when: The schema and the reference are read.
then: Events, commands with raises and checks, policies hearing one event, and command_change rows with a reason are in the schema and described.

title: A domain event's fields are its event_field rows in position order, as an entity's are
given: Event fields written out of position order.
when: They are loaded.
then: The fields come back in position order, only on events, in an entity field's shape.

title: A domain event with no fields is a gap, and a field without a name, or named twice, is refused
when: An event loses its fields; a field is blank, unnamed or named twice.
then: The event is a gap; the three fields are refused.

title: A command changes its own aggregate; another of its domain changed in the same transaction is recorded with its reason and listed as a recorded exception
given: A command change with a reason.
when: It is loaded, then given no reason, its own aggregate or another domain's aggregate.
then: The workspace lists the exception with its reason and reports no problem for it; the three bad rows are refused.

title: Requirements and rules may name a group, a column whose renaming changes no ID
when: A group is set on each of the five kinds, then renamed.
then: group_name is optional on all five; no ID changes and the renamed group loads.

title: Each test is of the test kind named after what it tests, and sits under that one record, which it proves
when: A use case test is removed, or written under another requirement.
then: Each test kind has one required parent named by its kind; only that requirement goes unproved.

title: A kind and a check open from where the Reader meets them
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reading a record opens its kind, a column and a problem code and lands on the format page each time, without leaving the workbench.
when: Open a record's page; choose its kind in the side bar, a column's label, and a problem's code.
then: Each opens its kind or check page in the same workbench, one step each.

title: The record actions take only a known action and a record ID, and find the data file themselves
when: Accepts each action with a record ID.
then: Refuses paths, unknown actions, lower-case and malformed IDs and extra keys; finds the data file whose row starts with the record's ID, never one that only names it, and again after it changes; and builds the native menu.

title: Open in editor uses VS Code by default, another known editor, the default app or a command of one's own
when: Reads settings with VS Code as the fallback, opens known editors by bundle ID on macOS and by command elsewhere, passes the file to a custom command as an argument and never in its text, and names the editor for the menu.

title: A standard sits under the product, its rules under it and their tests under each rule, and technical records meet a rule
when: A requirement or a test meets a rule; a link names a missing rule.
then: The standard, standard rule and standard rule test kinds, their stages, ID patterns and levels, and the meets pairs and labels are as stated and described; the three links are refused.

title: A standard rule is owed by the product, designed and built by the technical records that meet it and proved by its standard rule tests
given: A standard rule met by a technical record, with a standard rule test.
when: Its test is removed, not automated yet, or its file does not name it.
then: The rule counts outside every domain; without a valid test it is designed and built but not proved, and a test not automated yet is counted as such.

title: A standard rule that nothing meets is reported as not designed, not built and not proved; naming it in text does not meet it
given: A rule named only in a UI component's description.
when: It is loaded.
then: The rule is not designed and not proved, with a not-proved warning; no meets link exists.

title: A technical record sits under the one design record it implements and names its file; a file not there yet is work to do
when: A second handler for one command is written; a service's file is missing.
then: The second handler is refused; the missing file is a technical-file-missing warning and a built gap.

title: A table stores its name, its storage and its keys, its columns following from its record's fields
when: A primary key names an invariant; a table has no storage.
then: A table has no columns of its own, its name and storage are required and its keys are parts; both rows are refused.

title: An endpoint sits under the one command or query it exposes, and a step reaches it only through that command or query
when: An endpoint has no parent, or two; a step invokes an endpoint.
then: All three are refused.

title: A view or an integration has no owner and takes its product from its ID, and one no step uses is an error
when: Every link from a step to a view or an integration is removed; a view's ID names no product.
then: view-unused and integration-unused errors; the ID refused by id-prefix.

title: A rule of the interaction design is a view requirement under its view or an API requirement under its endpoint
when: A product is loaded.
then: The interaction design's only obligations are view and API requirements, under their view or endpoint, counted in coverage.

title: The merge keeps the rows both sides added, sorted
when: Merges a data file's base, ours and theirs.
then: Expects both sides' new rows in the merged file, sorted by key.

title: The merge takes a change or a removal made on one side only
when: Merges a data file's base, ours and theirs.
then: Expects the one side's change and removal in the merged file.

title: The merge keeps one copy of a row both sides added alike, and of a link both sides made
when: Merges a data file's base, ours and theirs.
then: Expects each row once.

title: lathe merge-data exits 1 with the clash on a real clash, and 0 on a clean merge
when: Merges a data file's base, ours and theirs.
then: Expects exit 1 naming the clash, and 0 for a clean merge.

title: The merge checks the merged table's own rules
when: Merges a data file's base, ours and theirs.
then: Expects a merged row that breaks its table's rules to fail the merge.

title: lathe merge-data writes the merge over ours, as git expects
when: Merges a data file's base, ours and theirs.
then: Expects the merged file written over ours.

title: Constraints sit under a value object, invariants under an aggregate, specifications have no owner and read one domain's aggregates, and policies sit under their command, each with a statement
when: A specification reads another domain's aggregate, and an invariant has no statement.
then: Constraints, invariants, specifications and policies have the parents and statements stated; both rows are refused.

title: Uniqueness is an invariant that the unique key enforcing it names, and only a unique key may name one
given: An invariant whose aggregate's data model names no file.
when: A unique key names the invariant.
then: The invariant is built through that key's table; a primary key or index naming an invariant is refused.

title: Read models with their fields and reads, queries of one read model, domain services that commands and queries call, and terms are in the schema
when: The schema and the reference are read.
then: Read models with fields and reads, queries of one read model, domain services that commands and queries call, and terms are in the schema and described.

title: The check prints errors, then warnings, then coverage with designed, built and proved
when: Runs `lathe check` on the broken-tests and unfinished fixtures.
then: Expects the errors section, then the warnings, then the coverage lines and each domain's tests line, each coverage line giving designed, built, proved and planned counts and the gaps.

title: The check exits 1 on any error and 0 otherwise, whatever the warnings
when: Runs `lathe check` on fixtures with errors, with no problems and with only warnings, and on a data file whose row has a column its table does not have.
then: Expects status 1, 0, 0 and 1, the last reporting `data-refused` with `data/product.jsonl:1`.

title: With --json the check prints the whole workspace
when: Runs `lathe check --json`.
then: Expects its output to parse to the same `Workspace` that `loadWorkspace` returns.

title: Data the store refuses loads no records, and each refusal is a data-refused error
when: Loads a product whose command names an aggregate that does not exist.
then: Expects no records loaded and every problem a data-refused error, naming the missing aggregate.

title: A link from a record of one product to a record of another is refused, whatever the relation; an ID in text is not a link
when: Adds an `involves` and an `applies` link from one product's records to another's, and loads text naming another product's ID.
then: Expects each link refused by `link-crosses-product`, and the text kept as written, with no link and no problem.

title: Data the store refuses is an error naming the file and line, not a crash
when: Runs lathe check on a product whose data/product.jsonl gives a column the table lacks.
then: Expects exit status 1 and a data-refused error naming data/product.jsonl:1.

title: Every problem names its check and, when it has one, its record
then: Expects every problem in every fixture to name its check in lower case with hyphens, to end as a sentence, and to name its record, whose ID its message contains.

title: A new check needs only a new check row
when: Adds one check row to a copy of the good fixture through the store, with no change to the engine.
then: Expects the row's problem as the workspace's only problem, named after the check.

title: Checks can read every typed table, with file facts already computed
when: Runs a check that counts the record registry, the links, the test table and the meta-model tables, and reads the file facts.
then: Expects the counts to match the workspace, and each file fact (the file exists, the test's file names its ID) to match the fixture.

title: A check reads the maxChildren setting from the product_setting table
when: Loads a product whose own check reads its `product_setting` row.
then: Expects the check to see `max_children` 3.

title: The record_group view covers a product kind's group_name and a flow step's path
when: Declares a product kind with a group_name field and adds records of it, grouped and ungrouped.
then: Expects record_group to give the grouped record its group as written, leave out the ungrouped one, and give a flow step its path.

title: Every check runs, in position order, even after one fails
when: Runs three check rows, the second of which reads a table that does not exist.
then: Expects their problems in position order, with the failing check reported as one error saying it could not run.

title: A use case with no flow is a coverage gap, never an error
when: Loads a use case with no flow.
then: Expects a use-case-without-flow gap in its domain, and no error.

title: A test at a level its kind does not allow is a warning
when: Loads a constraint test and a flow test at api.
then: Expects one test-level-not-allowed warning each, naming the levels its kind allows, and none for a constraint test at database.

title: A product relation declared twice is refused once
when: Loads a product relation written twice in its file.
then: Expects one primary-key refusal naming data/product_relation.jsonl, line 2.

title: A row taking another record's ID is refused once
when: Loads a use case test whose ID is a specification's, which links name.
then: Expects one unique-id refusal naming data/specification.jsonl:1, and none of the links to the ID.

title: An unknown parent is refused once
when: Loads a use case under a capability that does not exist.
then: Expects one foreign-key refusal: capability_id "EX-LEND-CAP09" names no capability.

title: A record that nothing uses is an error
when: Loads the complete product with no happens_in, exchanges_with, checks or renders links, and no field typed by its value object.
then: Expects one error each for the view, the integration, the value object, the specification and the UI component, saying to use it or remove it.

title: A link or parent the schema does not allow is refused once
when: Loads a renders link to a UC requirement, and a term with an aggregate_id column.
then: Expects one refusal saying the link names no view, and one column refusal for the column a term does not have.

title: A command's recorded exceptions are listed with their command, aggregate and reason, never as warnings
given: A command change with its reason.
when: The data is checked, and the check prints its text.
then: The workspace lists the exception, the text shows it under Recorded exceptions after the warnings, and no problem is reported for it.

title: An event a policy hears is delivered by outbox
A product check runs after Lathe's checks, against the same tables
when: Loads a product whose own check row reads the typed tables.
then: Expects its warnings after every problem from Lathe's checks, each with the severity its row gives.

title: A product check reports only on its own product's records, and on none
when: Loads two products, where one has a check that returns every domain and one row with no record.
then: Expects its problems for its own product's domain and for no record, and none for the other product's domain.

title: Without check rows of its own only Lathe's checks run
when: Loads the good fixture, which has no check rows of its own.
then: Expects no errors, and every problem from one of Lathe's checks.

title: A product check's name comes from its row, not from a check column its query returns
when: Loads a product check whose query returns `house-rule` in a check column.
then: Expects its problems under the row's name, `one-record-view-per-aggregate`, and none under `house-rule`.

title: A product check named like one of Lathe's checks is refused by the store, so it never runs
when: Adds a product check named `unproved` through the store, then writes the same row into the product's `data/check.jsonl`.
then: Expects a `primary-key` refusal naming Lathe's `lathe/data/check.jsonl`, then a `data-refused` error when the data loads, and the check never run.

title: A product check that fails to run is an error naming the check
when: Loads a product whose check `broken` reads a table that does not exist.
then: Expects one error with no record under `broken`, saying the check could not run.

title: A product names no checks folder: lathe.config.json refuses a checks setting, since checks are rows

then: Expects the rule proved in the first domain only, and not automated yet in the second once its test is.

title: A rule is not counted where every follower marks its setting not applicable
when: Both following use cases of a domain mark the rule's setting not applicable, then one gives a value; a rule with no setting is followed there too.
then: Expects only the rule with no setting counted, then both.

title: Not-proved warnings name the pattern rule and the domain
when: Two domains owe a rule and neither proves it, then one has a test not automated yet.
then: Expects one not-proved warning per domain naming the rule and the domain, the second time saying the test there is not automated yet.

title: A rule naming one of its pattern settings, or none, loads and is not reported
when: Loads a rule naming one of its pattern's settings with an applies-when setting, and a rule with no setting.
then: Expects both to load with no refusal, and no error on the fixture's pattern records.

title: A rule whose setting is not one of its pattern's settings is refused by the store
when: Loads a pattern rule naming a misspelled setting.
then: Expects a foreign-key refusal naming the file, the line and the setting.

title: A pattern that no use case follows is a warning
then: Expects a `pattern-not-followed` warning on a pattern with rules (saying how many are not counted) and on one with none, and none in a workspace where every pattern is followed.

title: An obligation outside every domain counts in Shared
when: Declares an obligation kind under the product, with one record.
then: Expects it counted and not proved in the product's Shared coverage, and no pattern rule there.

title: A rule no follower meets is waived in that domain
when: The rule applies only when the record is Loan, and the only follower's value is Tool.
then: Expects no count, gap or not-proved warning there, and a warning on its test there.

title: A test file names an ID only as a whole ID
when: Loads a test that proves `PX-D-DR03` while its file names only `PX-D-DR030` and `PX-D-DR03-R01`.
then: Expects a `proof-not-in-file` error.

title: A manual or planned test's file is checked only for existing
when: Loads a manual test naming a missing file, and a planned test naming an existing file that does not mention it.
then: Expects `test-file-missing` on the manual test, no error on the planned one, and no error from any other check.

title: Each domain counts its own tests by state, which every test gives
then: Expects 2 automated, 1 manual and 2 planned in one domain, 1 automated in another, zero in a domain with no tests and every test counted once, and the store to refuse a test with no state or with `Planned`.

title: lathe check reports each domain's tests by state
when: Runs lathe check on the complete product with one test not automated yet.
then: Expects one tests line for the domain, after all of its obligation lines.

title: A domain that follows a pattern itself owes every one of its rules, even where its use cases say not applicable
when: A domain follows a pattern itself while its one use case gives a rule's setting a not-applicable reason.
then: Expects that rule still owed there, with its `proves` gap and `unproved` warning naming the domain.

title: A domain follows a pattern itself or through any of its use cases
when: A domain follows a pattern itself and through its use case; another follows only through use cases that all mark the setting not applicable.
then: Expects the rule counted once in the first, and not at all in the second.

title: A pattern may have no settings
when: A pattern with no settings is followed by a domain and by a use case that gives no setting values.
then: Expects no pattern-setting-missing, and its rule owed.

title: A product's own kind may be an obligation
when: Declares one product kind an obligation and one not, with a record of each.
then: Expects the first counted, and not proved, and the second not counted.

title: The Tool Library still reads sensibly: its proof-only pattern rules are proved, with nothing asked for design
when: Loads this repo.
then: Expects TL-LEND to owe both Librarian action rules, all designed, built and proved, with no problem on the pattern's records.

title: A product kind named like one of Lathe's tables is refused
when: A product declares a kind named pattern_rule.
then: Expects the store to refuse it as a table name Lathe already has.

title: A use case that follows a pattern is not asked for requirements
when: Two use cases with no requirements, one following a pattern.
then: Expects use-case-without-requirement only for the one that follows nothing.

title: A pattern rule test in a domain that does not owe the rule is reported
when: Loads a pattern rule test naming a domain that does not follow the pattern, then one where the rule is waived.
then: Expects a pattern-rule-test-outside-followers error naming the domain and pattern, none once the domain follows it, and a warning where the rule is waived.

title: A manual test whose file names neither its ID, nor an ID it proves, nor its key is reported
then: Expects `manual-test-file-silent` on a manual test whose file is silent, and on one with a key the file lacks, naming the key.

title: The Reader sees how complete each domain is and what is undecided or broken
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Open a product's page in the app.
then: What the requirement says is on the page.

title: The Reader sees one obligation's chain alone in the graph
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Focus a UC requirement in the Graph view and turn on trace mode.
then: What the requirement says is on the page.

title: The Reader reads coverage for every obligation kind and every test state
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Open a domain's page and a gap's record.
then: What the requirement says is on the page.

title: The Reader sees which pattern rules a domain owes and how it stands on each
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Open a domain's Patterns we follow and a pattern's page.
then: What the requirement says is on the page.

title: The Reader sees each domain's tests by state beside its coverage
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Open a product's page and a domain's page.
then: What the requirement says is on the page.

title: The Reader sees what designs, builds and proves a record
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Open a UC requirement's page, then one of its tests.
then: What the requirement says is on the page.
